policy.genealogyAuthority: Canonical graph remains index.html; this register documents evidence and does not override it.
policy.religiousMaterial: Religious material from the Marion and Jay life-story source is excluded from their public biographies.

Reported James Webb Jr. parent couple

Cove Fort and Black Hawk War context

sources.title: East Hampton Congregational register gap review
sources.repository: Inherited Ancestry Atlas research log
supports: The surviving register series has a gap across the relevant baptism period
sources.limits: Exact archive catalog citation and register image range must be attached before final narration approval; the gap is not negative evidence.

sources.title: James W. Webb obituary
sources.repository: Owens Livingston Mortuary
supports: Jay left Vernon in 1943 to serve in the United States Army during the Second World War
Family-reported Bronze Star for actions in Germany
Return to logging work after the war
researchLeads: Family recollection that Jay may have participated in the D-Day invasion
sources.limits: The obituary does not identify Jay's unit, campaign dates or Bronze Star order. It supports Army service and a family-reported award but does not establish D-Day participation.

sources.title: Mormons at Mormon Dairy
sources.creator: E. A. Ames
sources.repository: U.S. National Archives and Records Administration
supports: Northern-Arizona Mormon family and settlement context during Jonathan Henry Webb's infancy
sources.limits: Photographed at Mormon Dairy near present-day Mormon Lake, not at Woodruff. The unidentified women and children are not represented as Webb relatives.

sources.title: Small Mormon store, northern Mex.
sources.creator: Bain News Service, publisher
sources.repository: Library of Congress, George Grantham Bain Collection
supports: Northern-Mexico Mormon settlement, clothing, horse and wagon context close to Jonathan Henry Webb and Della Ray's 1908 marriage period
sources.limits: The Bain caption identifies northern Mexico but not the specific colony. It is regional context only and is not represented as Colonia Morelos; the people are unidentified and are not claimed as Webb or Ray relatives.

sources.title: Atlas of the Mexican Conflict
sources.creator: Rand McNally and Company
sources.repository: Library of Congress, Geography and Map Division
supports: Period map base for the Arizona-Sonora borderlands during the Mexican Revolution
sources.limits: The original atlas does not document Jonathan and Della Webb's route, date of migration or motive. Pinedale and Colonia Morelos endpoint labels and the conceptual dotted connection were added by the project and must not be read as a proven itinerary.

sources.title: From Brutal Ally to Humble Believer: Mormon Colonists' Image of Pancho Villa
sources.creator: Brandon Morgan
sources.repository: New Mexico Historical Review, University of New Mexico Digital Repository
supports: Qualified regional context that Villa protected Mormon colonists' lives and property against Orozquista forces in Chihuahua in 1912, especially in the Colonia Díaz orbit
sources.limits: This does not establish a direct relationship with Jonathan Webb or Della Ray, does not concern Colonia Morelos in Sonora, and does not establish why or when their household moved to Arizona. Villa-colonist relations later became hostile and must not be simplified into a durable protective alliance.

sources.title: Forest stand
sources.creator: G. A. Pearson
sources.repository: USDA Forest Service Research Image Library
supports: Period mixed-forest context in Apache National Forest during the family's transition toward Arizona's White Mountains
sources.limits: The photograph is regional Apache National Forest context, not a documented view of Pinedale. No Webb family member is pictured.

sources.title: USGS Topo
sources.creator: U.S. Geological Survey, National Geospatial Program
sources.repository: The National Map
supports: Topographic context and geographic placement of Pinedale, Lakeside, Vernon, Snowflake and McNary in Arizona's White Mountains region
sources.limits: The five emphasized markers and labels were added by the project. They do not establish a migration route, chronology or person-specific residence beyond the claims separately supported in the family narrative.

sources.title: Original Snowflake Stake Academy
sources.creator: Unknown photographer
sources.repository: Mormon Settlement in Arizona via Wikimedia Commons
supports: The early Snowflake Stake Academy as a territorial educational institution and the institution-building context of Edward Milo Webb Jr.'s Arizona life
sources.limits: Edward opened the academy as its first principal and teacher in 1889 in an earlier log-cabin classroom. This photograph shows students at the later original dedicated academy building before its 1910 destruction; Edward is not identified among them.

sources.title: Sarah Elizabeth Carling Webb with five children
sources.creator: A. Miller, photographer
sources.date: 1891; reproduced in the 1969 first edition and 2017 second edition
sources.repository: Pioneer Women of Arizona, Religious Studies Center, Brigham Young University
supports: Sarah Elizabeth Carling Webb family context
Identification of Clark, Jonathan Henry (captioned Henry), Burr, Owen and Catherine in the 1891 photograph
Direct visual bridge from Edward Milo Webb Jr. through Sarah to Jonathan Henry Webb
sources.limits: The photograph is credited to A. Miller and the supplied copy to Flora Clark. Current research traces reproduction to the 1969 first edition of Pioneer Women of Arizona and the 2017 second edition, but does not establish first publication, copyright notice, photographer death or a rights transfer. It is approved by the project owner for the public, noncommercial family Atlas, but must be cleared or replaced before commercial distribution.

sources.title: Utah death-certificate index entry for Edward Milo Webb
sources.creator: Utah State Board of Health; indexed by FamilySearch
sources.repository: FamilySearch, Utah Death Certificates, 1904–1966
supports: Edward Milo Webb Jr. died 11 September 1921 in Murray, Salt Lake County, Utah
sources.limits: The indexed vital-record information is strong evidence, but the direct death-certificate image has not yet been attached to the Atlas evidence package.

sources.title: Map of the United States
sources.creator: U.S. Geological Survey
sources.repository: Library of Congress, Geography and Map Division
supports: Period geographic base for Edward Milo Webb Jr.'s westward life sequence through Missouri, the Platte corridor, Utah and Arizona Territory
sources.limits: Route lines, markers, labels and evidence legend were added by the project. The dashed 1852 line is a broad company corridor; the later solid connection shows chronological place sequence and does not claim exact roads.

sources.title: USGS Topo — western New York locator
sources.creator: U.S. Geological Survey, National Geospatial Program
sources.repository: The National Map
supports: Accurate geographic relationship of Hanover, Chautauqua County to Lake Erie, Lake Ontario, Chautauqua Lake and Buffalo
sources.limits: The map is modern and is used only as a locator for the 1815 birthplace. The project-added marker identifies a reference point within the town on land; no exact homestead or birth site is claimed.

sources.title: The American atlas, exhibiting the post offices, post roads, rail roads, canals, and the physical & political divisions of the United States of North America
sources.creator: David H. Burr; published by John Arrowsmith
sources.repository: Library of Congress, Geography and Map Division
supports: Period geographic context for the year Edward Milo Webb Sr. and Caroline Amelia Owens married
Named regional context spanning New York, Ohio, Illinois and Missouri
sources.limits: The project-added state labels identify regions named in the couple's early family history. No connecting line is drawn, and the image does not establish an exact route or marriage place.

sources.title: Nauvoo, Illinois, with temple on the hill
sources.creator: Attributed to Lucian R. Foster; true authorship not definitive
sources.repository: Public-domain historical image distributed through Wikimedia Commons
supports: Visual appearance of Nauvoo, Illinois, around 1846 during Edward Milo Webb Sr.'s documented Nauvoo period
sources.limits: The photograph is place context. No person in the image is identified as Edward or another Webb relative, and the photographer attribution is not treated as certain.

sources.title: An Evening Halt—Emigrants Moving to the West in 1840
sources.creator: Benjamin Franklin Reinhart
sources.repository: National Gallery of Art, Corcoran Collection
supports: People-centered visual context for nineteenth-century family migration, including clothing, household labor, children, wagons and livestock
sources.limits: The painting was created in 1867 as a retrospective representation of emigrants in 1840. It is not an eyewitness Webb-family scene, and no depicted person, animal, wagon, route or event is attributed to the family.

sources.title: 16th Company of 50 report
sources.creator: Brigham Young office; William B. Maxwell, company clerk
sources.repository: Church History Library, Brigham Young office emigrating companies reports, 1850–1862, CR 1234 5
supports: Edward Milo Webb Sr., Caroline Amelia Webb, Mary Jane Webb, Cordelia, Marcellus, Edward Jr. and young Caroline listed together in the Uriah Curtis Company report
James Hofer recorded as the continuation entry on the following manuscript image
sources.limits: The approved visual is a crop of manuscript image 9 and therefore does not show James Hofer, whose entry continues at the top of image 10. The report documents company membership and enumerated resources; it does not establish every later narrative detail of the journey.

sources.title: Crossing the Platte
sources.creator: Albert Bierstadt; published in Harper's Weekly
sources.repository: Library of Congress, Prints and Photographs Division
supports: Visual context for emigrant wagon travel across the South Platte in the decade of Edward Milo Webb Sr.'s final journey
sources.limits: The engraving was published seven years after Edward's 1852 death. It does not depict the Uriah Curtis Company, Edward's death or an identified Webb relative, and it does not establish a cause of death.

sources.title: Salt Lake City in 1850
sources.creator: Samuel Manning; engraving from American Pictures Drawn with Pen and Ink
sources.repository: U.S. National Archives and Records Administration, NAID 513336
supports: Visual settlement context for Salt Lake City shortly before Caroline Amelia Webb and the children arrived in September 1852
sources.limits: The engraving was published in 1876 and represents Salt Lake City in 1850. It does not depict Caroline, the Webb family or their precise arrival.

sources.title: Early Connecticut Marriages as Found on Ancient Church Records Prior to 1800 — Saybrook/Chester entries
sources.creator: Frederic W. Bailey, editor and copyist
sources.repository: Cornell University Library copy digitized by Internet Archive
supports: A James Webb and Elizabeth Douglas married on 9 December 1773 in the surviving Third Church of Saybrook, now Chester, marriage entries
The candidate couple existed together in the relevant Middlesex County locality before James Webb Jr.'s reported 1777 birth
sources.limits: This is a nineteenth-century published transcript, not the original register image. The editor states that most Third Church records had been lost. The marriage does not by itself identify the couple as James Webb Jr.'s parents.

sources.title: Heads of Families at the First Census of the United States Taken in the Year 1790 — Connecticut
sources.creator: United States Census Office
sources.repository: United States Government Printing Office copy digitized by Internet Archive
supports: A James Webb headed a household in Saybrook town in 1790
The same town enumeration includes multiple Webb households and a Daniel Douglass household, forming a useful locality cluster
sources.limits: The printed census names only household heads and does not state relationships. The page image and household columns must be inspected directly before demographic inference; this record does not connect the household to James Webb Jr.

sources.title: Connecticut Probate Estate Files Directory — Saybrook District
sources.creator: Connecticut State Library
sources.repository: Connecticut State Library
supports: The Saybrook Probate District directory contains a James Webb probate packet within the 1780–1880 Webb range
Chester probate matters were served by Saybrook Probate District
sources.limits: The directory identifies a retrieval target, not the decedent's identity, death date, heirs or relationship to James Webb Jr. The packet must be opened and abstracted before any genealogical conclusion.
